title: How the Tool Moves When the Joints Do: The Jacobian of an Arm in Three Dimensions, Checked Against Finite Differences, and Torque From Force

artifact.note: the geometric Jacobian of an arm in three dimensions: for each revolute joint its axis and a point on it (taken from the frame before the row in the standard convention and the frame after it in the modified one), the column z cross (tool point minus that point) over z, the tool's velocity from joint rates, the joint torques that balance a wrench at the tool (the transpose), and a finite difference Jacobian to check it against
